title: Evolution scales cell-level metabolic homeostasis into a tissue-level French flag axis

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolution scales cell-level metabolic homeostasis into a tissue-level French flag axis

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In a 2D neural cellular automaton in which each cell only pursues metabolic (energy) homeostasis and is rewarded according to how well its stripe matches the pattern, evolution (ES-HyperNEAT) produced cell collectives with tissue-level setpoints that solve the French flag problem, i.e. organize a body-wide three-valued positional information axis.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Our system showed the evolution of the much more complex setpoints of cell collectives (tissues) that solve a problem in morphospace: the organization of a body-wide positional information axis (the classic French flag problem in developmental biology).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Abstract”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata with gap-junction signalling, evolved with ES-HyperNEAT

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-01: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public code and explicit target metrics make the patterning result directly reproducible. The run can resolve the model behavior even if the higher-level interpretation remains debatable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run the public evolutionary neural-cellular-automaton code from homogeneous initial states and score final cell colors against the three-stripe target. Ablations can verify that only cell-level energy homeostasis is directly encoded while tissue patterning is evolved.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The reward function includes target-stripe information at the collective level.

The interpretation as scaling of goals is more theory-laden than pattern accuracy.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.98
analysis feasibility: 0.84
data adequacy: 0.92
operationalizability: 0.98
discriminating power: 0.92

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Pattern accuracy is a direct fitness readout, and the model code is public, so the French-flag result can be attempted without new biological data. The snapshot is not a complete reproduction package, and ES-HyperNEAT runs are slow and stochastic. A rerun can test whether such collectives arise, not recover every reported percentage from the original seeds.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rerun ES-HyperNEAT on the public 2D neural cellular automaton, with cell reward tied only to energy and stripe match, and measure whether the tissue reaches a three-band French-flag pattern. Reliable high pattern accuracy would support the scaling result in this model; consistent failure to pattern would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The repository sets a debug generation count and analysis expects a parameter file that is not in the tree.

Evolutionary runs are stochastic, so exact published accuracies need either saved genomes or many full replications.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.42
data existence: 0.68
